title: French courts split on forcing disclosure of Parcoursup's local university admissions algorithms
description: Parcoursup, France's national algorithm-driven platform matching secondary-school graduates to higher-education places since 2018, faced years of legal challenges over the opacity of the 'local algorithms' individual universities use to pre-sort applicants. After CNIL's March 2018 opinion pushed the ministry to publish the national algorithm's source code, student union UNEF sued for disclosure of universities' local algorithms; the Conseil d'État ruled in June 2019 that these were not subject to communication. The Conseil constitutionnel then held in April 2020 that a constitutional right of access to administrative documents required universities to disclose their selection criteria and reasoning, but only after admissions decisions were finalised — a partial transparency outcome that left the algorithms themselves undisclosed in advance of decisions.

history.note: Initial Edition 1.1 content. Legal history spans 2018-2020 across multiple distinct rulings; this record uses the Conseil constitutionnel's 3 April 2020 decision as the primary anchor since it is the most-cited resolution, but does not represent full closure of the underlying transparency question.

root_cause: French universities used locally-built ranking tools to pre-sort applicants without disclosing the criteria or logic, and the Conseil d'État found applicable law did not require disclosing these local processes in advance, prompting a constitutional challenge over the right of access to administrative documents.

citations.title: Décision n° 2020-834 QPC du 3 avril 2020 (Union nationale des étudiants de France)

relationships.reason: Parcoursup's automated, high-stakes sorting of applicants for a public service (higher education) without pre-decision disclosure is the same due-process concern DEC-004 addresses in welfare, grading, and debt-recovery contexts.
This incident extends the same genuine-human-review question into public education admissions.
